data.gender_notes: Juhi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'jwihi', meaning 'fair' or 'radiant'. In Hindu mythology, Juhi is a name of the river Goddess Ganga. It is also believed to represent the radiance of the moon. The name Juhi carries the meaning “Fair, Radiant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Juhi usually hope their child will grow to embody fair, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Juhi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fair, Radiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Juhi total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

vedic_reference.note: Juhi is a Sanskrit word meaning joy, happiness. It is derived from the Sanskrit word जीवन-सुख (jīvan-sukha) which means 'life's happiness'.

historical_references.reference: In Hindu mythology, Juhi is the name of a celestial nymph, a Yakshini, who was regarded as the goddess of beauty, youth, and long life. She was also known as the 'Goddess of Flowers'. According to legend, Juhi was created by the god Indra when he churned the ocean with the help of the demons and the gods to obtain the Amrita, the divine elixir of immortality. The gods and demons were engaged in a fierce battle during this process, and Juhi was born out of the churning process along with other divine beings.

Juhi is also a popular given name among Hindus in India. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'juhi', which means 'joy' or 'delight'. In the 18th and 19th centuries, the name Juhi became popular among the Rajputs and other warrior communities in Rajasthan and other parts of India. It was believed that bestowing the name Juhi upon a child would bring them joy, happiness, and success in their future endeavors.
